title: Formal Verification Write-Up POF 2828

canonical_node.axiom: The encoded ten-factor bridge matrix is internally coherent under Lean verification, conditional on the correctness of the encoded signatures.
definitions: C0 and C1: distinct coupling architectures.
C0 -> C1: one-way coupling step, irreversible relative to current transition definition.
Master Equation product: toy product that collapses to zero when any factor slot is zero.
LawIso: minimal binary abstraction match (value preservation, collapse preservation, bidirectional inverse mapping).
RichLawIso: enriched abstraction adding regime-role preservation, forward transition preservation, reverse transition reflection.

BridgeMatrix: module encoding ten factor slots G, M, E, S, T, K, R, Q, F, C with formal signatures, physical readings, spiritual readings, canonical bridge rows, targeted semantic swaps, and full toy product behavior.
derivation: Lean verifies C0 and C1 are distinct coupling architectures.
Lean verifies the one-way C0 -> C1 coupling step is irreversible relative to the current transition definition.
Lean verifies the toy Master Equation product collapses to zero when Q = 0.
Lean verifies Q != 0 is not sufficient for live coupling if another required factor is zero.
Lean verifies the stage sequence can reach redistribution from pre-localization and selected reverse one-step transitions are absent.
Lean verifies the named physics sequence maps to the named theology sequence by explicit order-preserving mapping.
The first LawIso model proved a two-state strong-force abstraction and a two-state love/agape abstraction match under value preservation, collapse preservation, and bidirectional inverse mapping.
Adversarial testing found a coin model with the same zero/one and collapse pattern also passed, exposing a false positive.
The richer RichLawIso layer added regime-role preservation, forward transition preservation, and reverse transition reflection.

RichLawIso accepts the enriched strong-force/love abstraction, rejects a natural coin model with random-low/random-high roles, but still accepts a deliberately relabeled coin model with constraining/liberating roles.
Lean verifies the ten canonical rows are internally consistent under the encoded signatures.

Lean rejects targeted substitutions: grace swapped with faith-commitment, entropy swapped with grace, compression swapped with communion, coherence swapped with consequence-lock, grace paired with entanglement as the physical reading.

Lean verifies full toy product behavior: every factor slot collapses the product when set to zero, R = 0 collapses the product, Q = 1 does not save the product if another required factor is zero, all ten factor slots set to 1 gives output 1.
canonical_node.action: Maintain the Lean formal verification sandbox as a working audit trail, and continue enriching factor signatures with equation-level invariants and adversarial tests to make the bridge proofs domain-faithful.
boundary: Does not prove that encoded physical readings are complete descriptions of the relevant physics.
Does not prove that encoded spiritual readings are complete descriptions of the relevant theological claims.
Does not prove that every row is a strict mathematical isomorphism in the strongest sense.
Does not prove the Master Equation over real-valued fields, functions, integrals, or Mathlib-backed analysis.
Does not prove empirical claims are true.
Does not prove that external citations support each encoded signature.
Does not prove that semantic labels are independently warranted.
Does not prove that physics and theology are structurally isomorphic in the full domain-rich sense.
test: Build cleanly with no active sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe.
Verify distinctness of C0 and C1.
Verify irreversibility of C0 -> C1 step.
Verify toy Master Equation product collapse when Q = 0.
Verify Q != 0 is not sufficient if another factor is zero.
Verify stage sequence reachability and absence of selected reverse one-step transitions.
Verify order-preserving mapping from physics sequence to theology sequence.
Run LawIso tests and adversarial coin false positive detection.
Run RichLawIso tests including rejection of natural coin model and acceptance of relabeled coin model.
Verify ten canonical rows internal consistency.
Verify rejection of targeted semantic substitutions.
Verify full toy product behavior including all factor slots set to 1 gives output 1.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a machine-checkable audit trail showing which structural claims are verified and which semantic grounding remains unproven, enabling adversarial testing of semantic substitutions.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the honest claim that the encoded bridge matrix is internally coherent and rejects several targeted semantic substitutions, conditional on signature correctness.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this formal verification write-up is removed, the framework loses its machine-checkable structural skeleton and the documented boundary between verified structure and unverified semantic grounding.

classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as honest formal verification sandbox; continue enriching signatures

overstatement_risks: Reading internal formal match as full external domain proof
Claiming Lean has independently proved structural isomorphism between physics and theology
Treating toy-model results as full domain proofs
kill_conditions: If Lean specifications are found to be too weak to carry the attached claims
If semantic labels are shown to be unfaithful to source domains
If the formal verification is used to claim empirical or theological truth
risk.lean_target: Encode equation-level invariants for each factor and add semantic-swap, same-domain wrong-mechanism, same-mechanism wrong-direction, and false-positive clone tests.

plain_summary: This document reports the current status of Lean formal verification for the ten-factor bridge matrix. It honestly states that Lean verifies internal coherence and rejection of certain semantic substitutions, but does not prove domain-faithful isomorphism. The main risk is overstating the formal results as full external proof. The recommended action is to continue enriching signatures and adversarial tests.
